name: Founders Pledge (charityevals)
beneficiaries_note: Moves money: each cause its members' and donors' money goes to, read live, brings its own countries.
summary: Founders Pledge runs a pledge community of entrepreneurs, researches where to give, advises members and ultra-wealthy Philanthropy Partners and runs donor-advised and public funds; this model covers its whole group's 2025 operating costs ($12.1M across its UK charity and US and German entities; the $317M of grants it passed on are the recipients' cost). At the defaults it averts about {{result}} years of healthy life per $1,000: of the $196M granted to its recommended charities in 2025, the site's shared share for a meta charity without a donor survey credits it with causing 30% of its funds' $55M and of its members' roughly $62M (half of that new money), and with redirecting 30% of its Philanthropy Partners' roughly $79M of advised giving, valued only for the gain and discounted for missing data (the one branch so discounted); each dollar is valued by its cause split, health (27.4%) at its grantees with a figure on the rankings (Evidence Action, Helen Keller Intl and four more), climate (31.5%) at Clean Air Task Force and SilverLining, catastrophic risks (2.8%) at SecureBio and education (31.1%) at the global-health charities, since none of its education grantees has a published model here. Its members' other giving it caused ($163M went to charities it doesn't recommend) adds about a quarter, at an ordinary charity's value. It moves about sixteen dollars to recommended charities for each dollar it spends. The result moves most with the next dollar ({{row:marginal_vs_past_average}} of the 2025 average) and the share of giving it caused; its climate third adds almost nothing.

sections.title: Cost
sections.explainer: What the modelled program cost in the year the outcomes below are counted for, including its share of overhead. From audited financial statements or the annual report.

sections.title: Reach
sections.explainer: How many people, animals or meals the spending reached in the same year, as the charity reports it.

sections.title: Effect per unit
sections.explainer: What the intervention does for each unit reached, from the best available studies, before any adjustment.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Career changes
sections.explainer: People the charity moves into high-impact jobs: per career changed, the pay they give up for the years they stay, valued at the new employer's live result per dollar, times the share of changes the charity caused (docs/normalization.md 2.8). The mirror of staff pay below market.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: The outcome in the family's shared unit, per dollar.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

sections.title: Value of a dollar moved (shared)
sections.explainer: charityevals' shared method for money a meta charity moves, the same rows in every such model (docs/normalization.md 2.8). A dollar moved is worth what the charities it reaches achieve, each at its live result on this site under your values; new money counts in full, shifted money only for the gain over where it would have gone.

rows.explainer: The year's flow of money to the charities it recommends, from all its channels: grants from members' donor-advised funds, its pooled funds, and Philanthropy Partners' giving on its advice. A flow against the year's cost (Convention 3): a past pledge fulfilled this year counts this year, and the period's new pledges ($1.54B from 275 members) aren't counted on top, so nothing is counted twice. Of the $359M its community gave in 2025, the other $163M went to charities it doesn't recommend: those count in a row of their own (other_giving_value).

source.quote: We welcomed 5 new partnerships in 2025, with a total $88M going to HIFO.

rows.explainer: Ultra-wealthy donors, mostly not members, for whom it researches questions and recommends charities. The sentence can be read as the new partnerships' giving or all partners'; either way it is giving it advised.

rows.label: Share of the partners' giving that went through its pooled funds (already counted there)
rows.explainer: Our judgment, 10% (0% to 55%). The sentence (accounts p. 5) is about five new partnerships in 2025. The $50M Climate Fund donation of 2025 came from a non-member who had already given $40M in 2024 (p. 9: '2024 saw a transformative $40m donation from a non-member … underlined this year by a second donation of $50m'), so not a new partner, and that gift was 'split between our Climate fund and supporting our operations' (p. 6). Some new partners may still have given through the funds; the high end is the reading that the $88M covers all partners, the Climate Fund donor among them.

rows.label: Partners' giving on its advice, outside its funds, 2025 (US$)
rows.explainer: The partners' giving less the part that went through its funds.

rows.label: Members' grants to its recommended charities from their own giving, 2025 (US$)
rows.explainer: The rest of the $196M: grants members recommended from their donor-advised funds at Founders Pledge, and other giving it records, to the charities it recommends. Never below $53M (all of the partners' $88M outside the funds).

rows.label: Share of members' giving to its recommended charities that Founders Pledge caused
rows.explainer: No published survey of its members: the shared figure for a meta charity without one (30%, 15% to 45%, from Giving What We Can's surveys of pledgers, 33% for its own pledgers). Its members give because they took its pledge and on its recommendations, but many would have given to good causes anyway; some of it is new giving (the pledge), some redirected (its advice), which the shared new-money share splits.

rows.label: Members' giving to its recommended charities that Founders Pledge caused, 2025 (US$)
rows.explainer: Members' grants to recommended charities × the share it caused, valued in the shared rows like pledgers' giving.

rows.label: Share of the partners' advised giving whose destination its advice changed
rows.explainer: No survey of the partners it advises: the shared figure for a meta charity without one (30%, 15% to 45%), read as the share of the advised money whose destination its advice changed, as for Longview's and Effektiv Spenden's advised giving. None of it counts as new money: partners are existing philanthropists giving anyway (templates.md: advice that changes where money is spent is all shifted).

rows.label: Partners' advised giving whose allocation its advice changed, 2025 (US$)
rows.explainer: Giving that would have happened anyway but went elsewhere because of its advice: all shifted money, valued in the shared rows by the gain over where it would have gone (informed_money_value).

rows.label: Fund and member giving to its recommended charities that Founders Pledge caused, 2025 (US$)
rows.explainer: Money moved it caused through its funds and its members' grants, valued in the shared rows net of where shifted money would have gone (new money in full); the partners' advised giving it redirected is informed_money.

rows.explainer: Unused: the policy branch is 0, so this row discounts nothing; kept so the canonical row exists.

rows.explainer: 0: the policy branch is empty (Founders Pledge wins nothing of its own; its value is the money it directs).

rows.label: Value of a dollar to the causes Founders Pledge directs money to (its 2025 split, live), units of value
rows.explainer: Where its recommended charities' 2025 money went by cause (its impact report, facts/meta.json fp_moved_2025_*): climate 31.5%, education 31.1%, health and economic empowerment 27.4%, global catastrophic risks 2.8%, by the site's rule for a split (normalization.md 2.8). Within each cause, its grantees with a model here, from its audited list of 2025 grants of £1M or more (note 10, facts/meta.json fp_grants_2025_*), each at its figure on the rankings under your values, weighted by their 2025 grants: health and economic empowerment at Evidence Action, Clinton Health Access Initiative, Fika, Precision Development, Helen Keller Intl (GiveWell's figures) and Save the Children (ours), its unmodelled grantees there (Raising the Village, Fortification Foundation and others) taking their average; climate at Clean Air Task Force and SilverLining; catastrophic risks at SecureBio, its one modelled grantee there. The accounts don't separate grants to its recommendations from members' other grants, so every modelled grantee of the cause on the list is read. Education charities are filed under global health and none of its education grantees has a published model here (the site's models of them are an unpublished evaluator's), so education takes the global-health charities on the rankings, equal weights (#cause:global-health). 'System change' (4.6%), 'global security' (1.0%) and the unlabelled slivers (about 1.6%): the chart gives no breakdown of them and no grantee can be placed in them with a source, so they take the average of the rest. The same split values the fund, member and partner money alike.

rows.label: Money its community gave to charities through its donor-advised funds, pooled funds and other channels, 2025 (US$)

source.title: Founders Pledge Ltd (charity 1162201), Trustees' Report and Consolidated Financial Statements for the year ended 31 December 2025 (audited, Crowe U.K. LLP)
source.quote: In 2025, our community guided more than $359M (£272M) to the charitable sector, through Founders Pledge's Donor Advised Funds (DAFs), Thematic Funds or other giving channels.
source.note: The impact summary gives the same $359M 'Moved to the charitable sector in 2025'.

rows.explainer: All giving through it, to recommended charities and others; the $196M to recommended charities is inside it.

rows.label: Share of its community's other giving that reached charities doing the work (not other donor-advised funds)
rows.explainer: Our judgment, 90% (80% to 100%), anchored on its audited accounts: grants outside its recommendations were about £92M in 2025 (£240.8M of grants, note 10, less the £149M to its recommendations, p. 4), and its list of grants of £1M or more shows about £9.3M of them to other donor-advised funds and grantmakers (Fidelity Charitable £6.2M, Daffy £1.5M, UBS Optimus Foundation £1.5M), about 10%, which pass money on to be granted again rather than to the work.

rows.label: Members' other giving, to charities it doesn't recommend, that Founders Pledge caused, 2025 (US$)
rows.explainer: Its community's giving outside its recommendations that reached end charities × the share it caused (the shared 30%); valued in other_giving_value, and its new half shares the credit with your dollar in donor_cost_share.

rows.label: Value of the other giving it caused, to charities it doesn't recommend (units of value)
rows.explainer: Its members' giving to charities it doesn't recommend ($163M in 2025), counted as Giving What We Can's model counts its donors' giving below its bar: the share it caused (the shared 30%), only the new half (shifted money between ordinary charities gains nothing), at an ordinary charity's value (the shared multiple of GiveDirectly's live result), after the share that reached end charities.

rows.label: Side effects of the money directed, as a share of its value
rows.explainer: Good and harm of its own beyond the money counted, its members' other giving being a row of its own (other_giving_value): its public research and funds followed by other platforms' donors (Effektiv Spenden's climate fund follows its Climate Fund) and its pledge norm among founders (positive); money parked in donor-advised funds for years (its restricted funds rose by £73M in 2025), donor attention drawn from other good uses and a few advisers steering much of a field's private money (negative). The recipients' own risks are in their figures already. 3% (−5% to +20%), our judgment, anchored on Giving What We Can's, Effektiv Spenden's and Longview's 5% for the same kind of effects, less here as the largest of them is counted in its own row.

rows.label: Share of money moved that is new money
rows.explainer: The site's one figure for every meta charity: about half the money moved wouldn't otherwise have been given (Ambitious Impact's Effective Giving Incubation report), from 35% to 80%.

rows.label: Value of a dollar moved, units of value
rows.explainer: Valued by where this organisation's money went: its own published split, each recipient at its live result on this site (value_destinations).

rows.label: Value of a dollar where shifted money would otherwise have gone (our judgment: an ordinary charity of each cause its money goes to, in its own mix), units of value
rows.explainer: Our judgment, the shared rule for an organisation whose money goes to several causes. Shifted money would have gone to an ordinary charity of the same cause: each cause's at the rule for a mover in that cause (GiveDirectly's live result, times a shared multiple, 1×, from 0 to 3×, over the global-health charities' on the rankings, times that cause's charities'), weighted by the organisation's own split, all live under your values.

rows.label: This charity's share of the good done with money, work or budgets it brings in
rows.explainer: The site's one setting for resources another party commits only because of the organisation (docs/normalization.md 2.24): the charity is credited this share of the good done with them, net of their cost; the rest stays with those who paid or did the work.

rows.label: Value of a dollar all shifted (given anyway, now to a better use), at the mobiliser's share, units of value
rows.explainer: Money that would have been given or spent anyway counts only for the gain over where it would have gone: a grantmaker's grants, or spending that research or advice changed. Its owners spent it, so the organisation is credited its share of that gain (mobiliser_share).

rows.label: Value of the spending its research or advice changed (all shifted money), units of value
rows.explainer: Spending its research or advice changed, at a judged share of the money it informed: all of it would have been spent anyway, so it counts for the gain over where it would have gone, discounted for weak evidence and for an outcome not measured for this charity (docs/normalization.md 2.8, 2.12).

rows.label: Value of a dollar moved, net of where shifted money would have gone, at the mobiliser's share, units of value
rows.explainer: New money counts in full; shifted money counts for the gain over where it would have gone. The donors gave it, so the organisation is credited its share of that good (mobiliser_share).

rows.label: Value of the money Founders Pledge moved and changed (units of value)
rows.explainer: Fund and member money it caused, net of where shifted money would have gone (new money in full), plus partners' giving its advice redirected, all shifted, after the evidence and missing-data steps, with the side effects; plus the other giving it caused, valued in its own row.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment (internal and external validity), a multiplier
rows.explainer: Applies to the partners' giving its advice changed (informed_money_value) and to the empty policy branch: how far the redirected giving does what its causes' ranked charities do, given that nobody measures what its advice changed. 0.7 (0.5 to 0.9), the template's figure, as for Longview's and Effektiv Spenden's advised giving.

rows.label: Share of the outcome that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: 1: what would have happened anyway is asked once, in the money rows (the share of fund and member money it caused, the share of advised money its advice changed, new against shifted money); the policy branch it would apply to is empty.

rows.label: This charity's share of the resources behind the outcome
rows.explainer: 1: the recipients' own costs and co-funders are inside each destination's figure per dollar; the policy branch is empty.

rows.label: Share of credit used
rows.explainer: The skeleton's policy branch, unused here (0): its share among co-advocates times the mobiliser's share (docs/normalization.md 2.24). The money moved and the careers take the mobiliser's share in their own rows.

rows.label: Counted less where the outcome isn't measured for this charity
rows.explainer: The site's missing-data discount (Convention 12): what its advice changed in partners' giving is judged, not counted, so the advised branch is thin; fund and member grants are counted in its audited books and take no discount.

rows.label: All adjustments combined
rows.explainer: The product of the adjustments above.

rows.label: Careers changed per year
rows.explainer: 0: Founders Pledge moves money, not people; it counts no career changes.

rows.label: Pay a career changer gives up per year (US$)
rows.explainer: The site's shared default (facts/meta.json) while careers_changed is 0: Founders Pledge changes no careers, so this multiplies nothing.

rows.label: Years a career changer stays in high-impact work
rows.explainer: The site's shared default (facts/meta.json) while careers_changed is 0: Founders Pledge changes no careers, so this multiplies nothing.

rows.label: Years a career changer stays, discounted
rows.explainer: Discounted at the shared rate.

rows.label: Value of a dollar of the new employers' work (units of value)
rows.explainer: Unused while careers_changed is 0; it reads the destinations the money goes to.

rows.label: Share of the career changes the charity caused
rows.explainer: The site's shared default (facts/meta.json) while careers_changed is 0: Founders Pledge changes no careers, so this multiplies nothing.

rows.label: Value of one career change (units of value)
rows.explainer: The site's one career-change step (docs/normalization.md 2.8), at the mobiliser's share (2.24): the person gives up the pay.

rows.label: Counted less where the outcome isn't measured for this charity
rows.explainer: Unused: no careers changed (careers_changed is 0), so this row multiplies nothing; kept so the canonical row exists.

rows.label: Value of the career changes (units of value)
rows.explainer: Unused while careers_changed is 0: the site's career-change step, kept so the canonical row exists.

rows.label: Total value (units of value)
rows.explainer: The adjustments apply to the empty policy branch; the money moved carries its own steps (own effect, new money, the advised branch's evidence and missing-data steps).

rows.label: Value per dollar
rows.explainer: For WELLBYs, rename the uov_* rows to wellbys_* and report in wellby. For animals, rename them to sads_* and add the species section of the corporate-campaign template (output ced_per_donor_dollar). For climate, start from the climate skeleton.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Staff pay over its operating costs (Convention 1).

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: The shared gap between what research and policy staff earn at a non-profit and what they could earn elsewhere (@staff_pay.gap_research_policy, {{row:salary_gap}}): its researchers and advisers come from finance, consulting and academia.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff (in-kind donation)
How much the next dollar does compared with the average dollar so far
rows.explainer: Founders Pledge's own figure (facts/next_dollar.json): {{row:marginal_vs_past_average}} (14–71%). The result is its 2025 average; it holds 20 months of operating costs in reserve, above its own 15-month minimum, and the next dollar goes to growing channels further from its members (Philanthropy Partnerships, non-member donors).

rows.label: Your dollar's share of the cost
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources: staff's forgone pay shares the outcome with your dollar. The donors whose money it moves give because of it: they are credited through the mobiliser's share, not here (docs/normalization.md 2.24).

rows.label: Units of value per dollar you give
